newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian Agroprombank okays share issue, SBS tie-in.
newsitem.headline: Russian Agroprombank okays share issue, SBS tie-in.

text.p: Russia's third-largest commercial bank, Agroprombank, said on Thursday that its board of directors had approved a 260 billion rouble share issue and planned to tie up with Stolichny Bank Sberezheny, a second large bank.
Sergei Meshcheryakov, spokesman for SBS-Agro, the name of the new entity uniting the two banks, declined to provide further details.
The new entity promises to be a giant on the Russian retail banking market.
Agroprombank was a specialised bank of the former Soviet Union and channelled credits to farmers and related industrial sectors such as food processing and farming equipment.
It has retained this profile and the present Russian government still uses it to channel credits to the sector, virtually dictating Agroprombank's credit policy.
Stolichny acquired a controlling stake in Agroprombank of 50 percent plus one share in a November 1996 tender when it took up a 130 billion rouble ($23.59 million) Agroprombank share issue.
The deal is not a full merger, since the two banks will operate as affiliates within one group.
Stolichny has been developing its retail banking operations to compete with Sberbank, the former Soviet monopoly savings bank, which still dominates the sector.
Stolichny plans a $1 billion, three-year modernisation programme for Agroprombank, which has 1,200 branches across Russia.
